distinguishes: When a ticket makes its claim valid: a message, both points in EIP-2537's encoding (padding zero, coordinates below p, c0 before c1), on their curves, in their subgroups and not at infinity, and the pairing check over the namespaced message. A verifier that skips the subgroup check (a valid signature plus a point of order 3 passes the pairing check alone) or the padding check, reduces a coordinate, takes compressed points, reads c1 before c0, or hashes without the namespace or its length byte, fails here.
provenance: Every signature comes from Commonware at c18a6b9 (cryptography's ops::sign_message, and ops::sign for the cases signed without a namespace, for MinSig), run as a program outside this repository, each valid one also issued blind there and found equal; its points are written here in EIP-2537's encoding. Every verdict on steps 3 and 4 is the Hegota testnet's EIP-2537 pairing precompile (eth_call to 0x0f, 2026-10-20) on the signature, the negated generator of G2, Commonware's H(u) and the issuer: true, false, or an error for an input it refuses. Step 1 is applied by hand. Issuer A's and B's secret keys are the SHA-256 of 'exp-mempool-l2s claim ticket issuer A' and '... issuer B' reduced modulo the group order. Two cases are tickets the testnet mined, with their issuers' keys: one from exp-frames f0749cb, signed under that run's namespace, and one from the re-run under FRAME_TICKET_V1 (kohaku-rs eea02a3), which verifies.
